scplotter to work with Slide-seq data prepared by Giotto¶

The technology. Slide-seq and Slide-seqV2 deposit a lawn of barcoded beads about 10 um across on a puck, then place a tissue section on top. RNA captured by each bead is sequenced, giving near-single-cell resolution without any microscopy — there is no tissue image at all, so spatial plots are drawn on bead coordinates.

What this notebook covers. Building a Giotto object from a bead-location table plus a beads-by-genes matrix, filtering and normalising, clustering, and plotting. Because there is no image, it is a good example of how much of a spatial figure can be carried by points and cluster colour alone.

Data. Mouse cerebellum (Slide-seqV2). The mouse-brain puck originally referenced by the Giotto tutorial lives on NeMO, which is unreachable from many networks; the cerebellum set has the same shape — bead coordinates plus a counts matrix — and is the substitute used here.

Before you run. A Giotto Python environment for the clustering calls.

Upstream tutorial.

  • https://giottosuite.com/articles/slideseq_mouse_brain.html

Go back to scplotter documentation: https://pwwang.github.io/scplotter/

library(Giotto)

# Ensure Giotto can access a python env
genv_exists <- suppressMessages(checkGiottoEnvironment())
print(genv_exists)

python_path <- Sys.getenv("GIOTTO_PYTHON")
Sys.setenv(RETICULATE_PYTHON = python_path)

invisible(capture.output(suppressMessages(set_giotto_python_path(python_path = python_path))))

library(Giotto)

## Set instructions
results_folder <- "data/Giotto_SlideSeq.results"

instructions <- createGiottoInstructions(
    save_dir = results_folder,
    save_plot = FALSE,
    show_plot = TRUE,
    return_plot = TRUE,
    python_path = python_path
)

## Provide the path to the visium folder
data_path <- "data/Giotto_SlideSeq"

expression_matrix <- local({
    dge <- data.table::fread(file.path(data_path, "MappedDGEForR.csv"), header = TRUE)
    m <- as.matrix(dge[, -1, with = FALSE])
    rownames(m) <- dge[[1]]
    m
})
spatial_locs <- data.table::fread(file.path(data_path, "BeadLocationsForR.csv"))

spatial_locs <- spatial_locs[spatial_locs$barcodes %in% colnames(expression_matrix),]

giotto_object <- createGiottoObject(
  expression = expression_matrix,
  spatial_locs = spatial_locs,
  instructions = instructions
)

force(giotto_object)

giotto_object <- filterGiotto(giotto_object,
                              min_det_feats_per_cell = 10,
                              feat_det_in_min_cells = 10)

giotto_object <- normalizeGiotto(giotto_object)
giotto_object <- addStatistics(giotto_object)
giotto_object <- runPCA(giotto_object)
giotto_object <- runUMAP(giotto_object,
                         dimensions_to_use = 1:10)
giotto_object <- createNearestNetwork(giotto_object)

giotto_object <- doLeidenCluster(giotto_object,
                                 resolution = 1)
